newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's northern crude port partly reopened.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's northern crude port partly reopened.

text.p: State-owned Chinese Petroleum said on Monday it had reopened one of two unloading units at its north Taiwan crude port, allowing 200,000 tonnes of oil to replenish the Taoyuan refinery's dwindling supply.

"We already started offloading crude oil through one of the two units," a Taoyuan refinery official confirmed to Reuters by telephone. "A total of about 200,000 tonnes of crude has been piped into Taoyuan refinery."

The tanker Vanadis, which had waited for a week to unload its 300,000-tonne cargo of African crude and had assisted with the repairs, was the source of the new crude but was forced by rough seas to stop, the official said.
"We cannot finish the offloading because the remaining crude is not heavy enough to keep the tanker stable in the current weather and sea conditions," he said.
The Vanadis was expected to offload its remaining crude after the weather improved or be redirected to Chinese Petroleum's southern crude port at Kaohsiung.

Chinese Petroleum around September 16 closed both of the northern port's unloading units due to unspecified pipeline problems, halting supplies to the company's only north Taiwan refinery and threatening supplies of jet oil, its main product.
Concern over low crude supplies on hand in turn forced the company to shut down one the refinery's two distillation units to slow production.
